# Bug report

## Describe the bug

Hi, I currently maintain [next-seo](https://github.com/garmeeh/next-seo) and I am in the process of testing [V2](https://github.com/garmeeh/next-seo/pull/53) of the library. I noticed that on the latest version of next that when navigating to another page the head does not update correctly. I started back at V7 of Next worked up to the version it stopped working on.

The last version it works on is [v8.0.4-canary.19](https://github.com/zeit/next.js/releases/tag/v8.0.4-canary.19) and as soon as I update to [v8.0.4-canary.20](https://github.com/zeit/next.js/releases/tag/v8.0.4-canary.20) it stops working. Looking through the commits associated with the version it doesn't seem that they would cause an issue. Any insights that would help debug?


Basic scenario:

Hope to publish a canary version later of next-seo and provide an example sandbox with the steps to reproduce.

Important to note: app [explicitly depends on `react-ssr-prepass`](https://github.com/iamstarkov/topics-manager/blob/master/package.json#L26)

## To Reproduce

* Working v8 demo https://topics-manager.now.sh/ (master)
* Failing v9 demo https://topics-manager-phz67x2ki.now.sh/ (only one bump commit ahead of master)

I cant replicate error locally, because next.js is set to `serverless` mode. Furthermore, i use `now dev` and didnt see `local prod` mode of it too. Is there any documentation on how can one debug production-only problems like this?

Maybe, i lack context and some documentation. If someone can help with those, then perhaps i can try try to fix this issue on my own

items.title: [v9 regression] Can't render a page as a response to POST anymore
items.body:
# Bug report

## Describe the bug

Hi! 
Since Next.js v9, we are no longer able to render a page as a response to POST request anymore. Basically, everything seems to be going fine on the server, but when it comes to rendering the page, Next throws a 405 error. We believe it's due to this line of code: https://github.com/zeit/next.js/blob/fce7e4eaee45e89557ceaa81fbd42057f8596e22/packages/next-server/server/next-server.ts#L509

## To Reproduce

Here's an example of a flow that leads to the error. We are using custom Express server, and serving static nojs pages which can only use forms to submit data, and we don't keep any server-side state.

1. `GET` to `/nojs/settings` -> handled by `server.get("/nojs/settings"...)` -> renders `/nojs/settings` page.
2. To change settings, user `POST`s a form to `/nojs/settings` -> handled by `server.post("/nojs/settings"...)`
3. Server needs to respond with the page that has some additional data (error messages etc.) passed as `queryParams`. So after whatever needs to be done to get that data, `server.post("/nojs/settings"...)` is doing `app.render(req, res, "/nojs/settings", { data })`
4. User is going to see the `_error.js` page with `405` error code.

## Expected behavior

Before v9, `app.render()` on `POST` request used to render a page without any problems. 
Support for this behaviour is needed to serve static nojs pages, that only use forms to submit data, without introducing server-side state.
This is a major regression for this rather standard web practice use case and because of that we're stuck back on v8.

items.title: Performance Mark regression
items.body:
# Bug report

## Describe the bug

Upgrading from Next 9.0.3 to 9.0.4 breaks our performance mark measurements.
I haven't done a git bisect or any further investigation but I suspect [this](https://github.com/zeit/next.js/pull/8069/files#diff-3578818137c8db2e46579427372768d0R293) to be the root cause (as it clears all marks).

## To Reproduce

1. Clone, install and run dev script https://github.com/damianfrizzi/nextjsperformancemarkregression
2. Open devtools console and look for the performance mark `performance.getEntriesByName('bla')` -> There is no entry
4. Downgrade next to 9.0.3
5. Open devtools console and look for the performance mark `performance.getEntriesByName('bla')` -> There is an entry

## Expected behavior

Performance marks defined in user land shouldn't be overwritten/deleted.

items.title: Regression of #14740
items.body:
# Bug report

## Describe the bug

The work in #14740 has caused a bug when a page errors on the server side

```
Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read property 'statusCode' of undefined
    at Object.fLxa (index.js:60)
    at t (bootstrap:86)
    at Object.LwBP (next.js:1)
    at t (bootstrap:86)
    at c (bootstrap:45)
    at Array.a [as push] (bootstrap:32)
    at 84f3b8c7222dd2225c268a644154c5ba8e99769e.f6885231c259f16e58e7.js:1
```

Inspecting the error it's happening with:

```
if (
  page !== '/404' &&
  !(
    page === '/_error' &&
    hydrateProps &&
    hydrateProps.pageProps.statusCode === '404'
  )
) {
  asPath = delBasePath(asPath)
}
```
Namely `hydrateProps` does not have a `pageProps` at this moment. All it has is `initialProps`, `initialState` and `isServer`

`pageProps` should be prefixed with `initialProps`

EG the full line should be

`hydrateProps.initialProps.pageProps.statusCode === '404'`

## To Reproduce

Generate an error server side.

```
function App() {
	const [s, setS] = useState({});
	const z = useMemo(
		() => ({
			a: s.g.h, //.h is not defined
		}),
		[s.g.h]
	);
```

## Expected behavior

Should not throw an exception here

## Screenshots
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/564256/89461991-9c09c500-d721-11ea-972d-ed488eed3346.png)

## System information

- OS: macOS
- Version of Next.js: 9.5.1
- Version of Node.js: 12.18.2
